subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool upsize and throughput sizing proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Ramos <kate@furnishinc.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@furnishinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool upsize and throughput sizing proposal

Hi Kate / Rafael,

Following up on our renewal conversation last week. Attached is a concise proposal (Furnish_Dedicated_Proposal_v3.pdf) and a simple throughput model (furnish_qps_growth_model.xlsx) that I built with Dev. High-level summary:

- Current committed pool: 8 GPUs (A100-class equivalent)
- Current observed baseline QPS (30-day avg): ~42 QPS, median tokens per request: ~140
- Forecasted business growth next 12 months: +2.2x median QPS under product roadmap and marketing plans (see model)
- Renewal ask (recommended): reserve 16 GPUs with a 20% burst buffer (practical pool = 19 GPUs) to cover projected peak QPS and 95th percentile spikes while preserving latency SLOs

Why this number: the attached model assumes a conservative per-GPU p95 throughput of ~10 QPS at your median token size for the primary gen model we run. With projected peak QPS of ~160, that maps to 16 GPUs. We recommend the 20% buffer to handle short-lived campaign spikes and to avoid throttles.

Commercials: 12-month committed term gives an increased discount vs month-to-month; I put an illustrative pricing line in the PDF with an 18% commitment discount and a separate short-term burst billing mechanism for overage.

Next steps. If you’re aligned on the sizing and term (12 months), I’ll:
- Lock pricing and produce an updated quote + DocuSign (Marissa on copy to help finalize)
- Share the annotated throughput model with Dev team for dry-run load tests
- Schedule a 30-min walkthrough to validate assumptions

Please flag anything you'd like us to change in the assumptions. If you prefer a shorter 6-month commit we can run a smaller initial bump and schedule a mid-term re-evaluation.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Kate Ramos <kate@furnishinc.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@furnishinc.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool upsize and throughput sizing proposal

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the model. A few clarifying questions before we lock a term: 

1) Per-GPU assumptions — you list ~10 QPS p95 at our median token size. Does that include KV/prefix caching for our interactive flows, or is that a cold-start number?
2) Bursting and failures — what happens if we spike to 2.5x the projected peak for 15 minutes? Will traffic get queued/throttled or will you route to hosted fallback variants? How does that affect latency guarantees?
3) Cost delta — can you show the monthly delta vs our current spend so we can justify to procurement? We need an explicit monthly $ number (not just %).
4) SLA details — we need a clear statement on throughput SLO and crediting model if you miss p95 latency under committed capacity.

If you can fold answers into the updated quote that would help speed approvals. Rafael and I are available for a 30-min call Thurs morning.

—Kate
Head of Product Operations | Furnish Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Ramos <kate@furnishinc.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@furnishinc.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool upsize and throughput sizing proposal

Kate — great questions, answered inline below and I’ve pulled the relevant lines into the proposal and the model (see attachment). Quick TL;DR at top.

TL;DR
- Per-GPU p95 QPS figure of ~10 assumes steady-state with KV/prefix caching in place (your interactive flows benefit significantly from prefix cache hit rates we observed in May). Cold-start without cached KV has lower throughput (~6 QPS p95).
- For short, sharp spikes (<=30 minutes) we will: 1) route excess to your hosted-compatible variant (identical model but lower priority), and 2) honor latency SLO for requests served by reserved pool; requests routed to fallback will have higher latency but will still be served. We include a burst billing mechanism for overage minutes.
- Monthly cost delta (illustrative): current committed spend for 8 GPUs: $48,000/month. Proposed 16-GPU reserved pool: $90,000/month after commitment discount (12-month term). Incremental delta = $42,000/month. Exact quote attached in PDF.
- SLA: we guarantee p95 inference latency target of 450ms for requests served from the reserved pool up to committed QPS. Missed SLOs qualify for credits per the SLA table in the proposal.

Sizing notes / math (excerpt from model):
- Assumptions:
  • Median tokens/request: 140 (your telemetry)
  • Projected peak QPS at renewal (12-month outlook): 160 QPS
  • Safe target (peak + 20% buffer): 192 QPS
  • Per-GPU p95 QPS at median token size (with caching): 10 QPS
- GPUs required = ceil(192 / 10) = 20 GPUs.
- Current reserved = 8 GPUs -> recommended upsell = +12 GPUs to get to 20.

Note: The earlier email’s 16 GPU figure assumed a slightly higher per-GPU capacity; after re-running model against your actual token distribution and our internal p95 baselines, 20 GPUs is the safer committed target. We show a step plan in the model:
- Option A (recommended): Commit to 20 GPUs for 12 months, 18% discount, 20% burst buffer handled by short-term burst billing.
- Option B (conservative): Commit to 14 GPUs for 6 months, revisit at month 4 with telemetry; this reduces immediate delta to +6 GPUs but requires a mid-term re-eval.

Operational items I asked Dev to validate (Dev, any red flags?):
- Run a 2-hour stress test at 140% projected peak next week against a mirror of Furnish traffic (we can coordinate the test window).
- Confirm autoscaling and routing policies (how fast we move to hosted-fallback during sustained pressure).

Attached: updated proposal PDF and the live XLSX with per-hour QPS projections + GPU calc rows.

If this looks good, I’ll have Marissa produce an updated quote and DocuSign. Rafael / Kate — are you OK locking Option A or do you prefer Option B? Happy to talk through trade-offs on Thursday.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
